stem: A healthy 31-year-old woman comes to the office as she desires a second child.  Her first child, who was conceived via donor insemination, was recently diagnosed with a rare autosomal recessive disease that affects 1 in 40,000 individuals.  The carrier frequency in the general population is 1 in 100; genetic testing confirms the woman is a carrier for the disease.  A different sperm donor is selected with no personal or family history of the disease; however, his carrier status is unknown.  Which of the following is the most likely probability of the woman conceiving an affected child with the new sperm donor?​‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌​​​​​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​​​‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​​​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌​​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​​​‌‌​​​​‌​‌​​​‌​‌
explanation:
For autosomal recessive disorders, children must inherit a mutant allele from each parent in order to be affected.

For 2 healthy parents to conceive an affected child (aa), they must each be a carrier for the disease (Aa).  Therefore, the probability of conceiving an affected child is equal to the probability of both parents being carriers multiplied by the probability of the child independently inheriting a mutant allele from each carrier parent:

P(affected child) = P(carrier mother) × P(carrier father) × P(both parents transmitting a mutant allele)

  • P(carrier mother):  The probability of the woman being a carrier is 1 because she is a known carrier.

  • P(carrier father):  The sperm donor's genotype is unknown, and he has no personal or family history of the disease.  Therefore, the probability of the sperm donor being a carrier is equal to the carrier frequency in the general population, or 1 in 100.

  • P(both parents transmitting a mutant allele):  Assuming both parents are carriers, then the probability of both parents independently transmitting a mutant allele is (1/2) × (1/2), or 1/4.

P(affected child) = 1 × 1/100 × 1/4 = 1 in 400

Therefore, the probability of the woman conceiving an affected child is 1 in 400.

Educational objective:The probability that two healthy parents will conceive a child with an autosomal recessive disorder is equal to the probability of both parents being carriers multiplied by the probability of the child independently inheriting a mutant allele from each parent.  If a parent's genotype is unknown, then the probability of that parent being a carrier is equal to the carrier frequency in the general population.​‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​‌​​​​​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​​​‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌​​​​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌​​‌‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌​​‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌​​‌​‌​​​‌‌​​​​‌​‌​​​‌​‌
